I've put together a first-pass offer (offer_draft_v1.docx attached) for Jordan. Key points to review:
- Base band: $190k–$210k (role level: Sr Product Manager II) — I put $200k as the proposed base.
- Signing bonus: $25,000 gross, pro-rated if start after 30 days.

Subject: Re: Offer draft for Jordan — please review redlines (attached)

Monica — thanks for the draft. A few manager notes:
- Base: $200k is fine. If we can't secure $200k, we should keep offer flexibility down to $195k without needing re-approval.
- Signing bonus: manager prefers proration language tied to payroll cycle rather than a hard 30-day cutoff — e.g., "pro-rated based on days worked in the first pay period following start". That avoids awkward mid-payroll splits.
- Staged start: we can do a staged 0.6 FTE first 30 days for onboarding if candidate needs to finish an existing project, but compensation should be pro-rated accordingly and the start date recorded as the first paid day for vesting/equity purposes.

Please update the draft with the payroll-tied proration and explicit note that the formal start date for vesting/equity is the first paid day.

Marcus
Director, Product Management

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Novak <elena.novak@hiringadvisors.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Offer draft for Jordan — clawback wording and payroll proration

Thanks — a couple HR/legal suggestions:
1) Clawback: we should avoid a 12-month absolute reclaim for discretionary signing bonuses. Suggested clause: "If the employee voluntarily resigns within six (6) months of the start date, the employee agrees to repay the signing bonus on a pro-rated basis (i.e., repayment amount = bonus * (6 - months_employed)/6). Exceptions may be approved in writing by People Ops." This is consistent with other recent offers and reduces legal risk.
2) Proration: wording I recommend: "Signing bonus policy: For hires who begin mid-pay period, signing bonus will be prorated to reflect the portion of the initial payroll period worked and paid on the first payroll following the employee's official start date." That aligns with payroll operations.
3) Vesting: reiterate that equity vesting schedule begins on the first paid day; include a fallback for remote hires to ensure RSU delivery addresses tax withholdings.

I'll draft the exact clause language and add tracked changes to the attached doc if you want.

Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
